quests.question: You may borrow the equipment ____ you return it in the same condition.
quests.sentence: You may borrow the equipment ____ you return it in the same condition.
quests.hint: There is one specific condition for borrowing - the item must come back undamaged.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a formal condition that must be met for permission to apply. 'You may borrow it provided that you return it undamaged' = 'on the condition that it comes back undamaged'. 'Provided that' is more formal than 'if'.

quests.question: ____ the current growth rate continues, profits will double within five years.
quests.sentence: ____ the current growth rate continues, profits will double within five years.
quests.hint: The current growth rate is an acknowledged fact being used as a basis for projection.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces a premise or acknowledged fact as the basis for a conclusion. 'Given that growth continues at this rate' = 'taking this fact as the basis' or 'because this is true'. It is more formal than 'since' or 'because'.

quests.question: The team can choose any approach ____ the project is delivered on time.
quests.sentence: The team can choose any approach ____ the project is delivered on time.
quests.hint: On-time delivery is the one non-negotiable condition for full creative freedom.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets a formal condition for permission. 'Any approach is acceptable provided that the deadline is met' = 'on condition that the deadline is met'. The freedom is unlimited EXCEPT FOR the one requirement.

quests.question: She will continue to support the charity ____ her financial situation does not change.
quests.sentence: She will continue to support the charity ____ her financial situation does not change.
quests.hint: Her support continues on the condition that her finances stay stable.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a continuing condition. 'She will support as long as her situation doesn't change' = 'on the continuing condition that her finances remain stable'. 'As long as' implies the condition must remain true over time.

quests.question: ____ the merger creates significant job losses, the union will support it.
quests.sentence: ____ the merger creates significant job losses, the union will support it.
quests.hint: 'Unless' - significant job losses are the one thing that would lose union support.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the single exception. 'The union will support it unless it creates job losses' = 'the union will only oppose it if it DOES cause job losses'. 'Unless' is the clearest connector for this 'except if' condition.

quests.question: ____ the complexity of the issue, a quick resolution seems unlikely.
quests.sentence: ____ the complexity of the issue, a quick resolution seems unlikely.
quests.hint: The complexity is an acknowledged fact being used to reach a conclusion.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an acknowledged premise used as the basis for a logical conclusion. 'Given that the issue is complex' = 'taking the complexity into account' or 'because the issue is so complex'. This formal connector acknowledges a fact and draws a conclusion from it.

quests.question: The student may retake the exam ____ they submit the application within thirty days.
quests.sentence: The student may retake the exam ____ they submit the application within thirty days.
quests.hint: Submitting the application within thirty days is the formal condition for retaking.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets a formal, administrative condition. 'May retake provided that the application is submitted within thirty days' = 'on the condition that the timing requirement is met'. This is formal language for official conditions.

quests.question: I am happy to work overtime ____ I receive time off in lieu.
quests.sentence: I am happy to work overtime ____ I receive time off in lieu.
quests.hint: Receiving time off in lieu is the ongoing condition for willingness to work overtime.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a continuing condition for ongoing agreement. 'Happy to work overtime as long as I receive compensation' = 'on the continuing condition that the compensation is provided'. If the compensation stops, the agreement ends.

quests.question: ____ the candidate's experience, the salary offer seems surprisingly low.
quests.sentence: ____ the candidate's experience, the salary offer seems surprisingly low.
quests.hint: The candidate's impressive experience is the acknowledged fact that makes the salary seem wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an acknowledged fact used to evaluate a situation. 'Given the candidate's experience' = 'taking into account their experience' or 'considering how experienced they are'. The experience (premise) makes the low salary (conclusion) seem inappropriate.

quests.question: The loan will be approved ____ the applicant meets all the eligibility criteria.
quests.sentence: The loan will be approved ____ the applicant meets all the eligibility criteria.
quests.hint: Meeting all eligibility criteria is the formal condition for loan approval.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a formal condition in financial or legal language. 'Will be approved provided that criteria are met' = 'on condition that all requirements are satisfied'. This is standard formal conditional language in banking.

quests.question: She will keep the information completely confidential ____ she is asked to disclose it legally.
quests.sentence: She will keep the information completely confidential ____ she is asked to disclose it legally.
quests.hint: Legal disclosure is the one exception to her confidentiality commitment.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the one exceptional circumstance. 'Will keep it confidential unless legally required to disclose' = 'will keep it secret EXCEPT IF the law requires disclosure'. One exception, otherwise absolute confidentiality.

quests.question: ____ the amount of data available today, machine learning systems can be extraordinarily accurate.
quests.sentence: ____ the amount of data available today, machine learning systems can be extraordinarily accurate.
quests.hint: The abundance of data is the acknowledged fact that makes ML accuracy possible.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces the premise upon which the conclusion is based. 'Given that enormous amounts of data exist today' = 'because this data is available'. The data (premise) enables the accuracy (conclusion).

quests.question: Staff may work flexible hours ____ core working hours of ten to three are always covered.
quests.sentence: Staff may work flexible hours ____ core working hours of ten to three are always covered.
quests.hint: Covering core hours is the non-negotiable condition for flexible working.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets the formal condition for a workplace agreement. 'May work flexible hours provided that core hours are covered' = 'on condition that the essential hours requirement is always met'. This is typical HR policy language.

quests.question: He will maintain his position on the board ____ he retains shareholder confidence.
quests.sentence: He will maintain his position on the board ____ he retains shareholder confidence.
quests.hint: Shareholder confidence is the ongoing condition for remaining on the board.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a continuing condition for an ongoing arrangement. 'Will maintain his position as long as he has shareholder confidence' = 'on the continuing condition that confidence is not lost'. The moment confidence goes, so does the position.

quests.question: ____ the patient's age and medical history, the consultant recommended a less invasive treatment.
quests.sentence: ____ the patient's age and medical history, the consultant recommended a less invasive treatment.
quests.hint: The patient's age and history are the acknowledged factors that shaped the recommendation.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces the relevant facts that justify a clinical decision. 'Given the patient's age and history' = 'taking these factors into consideration'. The specific circumstances (premise) determine the treatment choice (conclusion).

quests.question: The contractor may begin work on Monday ____ all permits are in place by Friday.
quests.sentence: The contractor may begin work on Monday ____ all permits are in place by Friday.
quests.hint: All permits being in place by Friday is the condition for Monday's work to start.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a formal condition with a deadline. 'May begin on Monday provided that permits are in place by Friday' = 'on the condition that the legal requirements are met before the start date'. Standard contractual language.

quests.question: She will accept the posting abroad ____ her family can accompany her.
quests.sentence: She will accept the posting abroad ____ her family can accompany her.
quests.hint: Her family coming with her is the ongoing personal condition for accepting.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a personal condition for agreement. 'Will accept the posting as long as her family can come' = 'on the continuing condition that her family is with her'. Without this, she would not go.

quests.question: ____ the scale of the damage, the insurance company is likely to declare it a write-off.
quests.sentence: ____ the scale of the damage, the insurance company is likely to declare it a write-off.
quests.hint: The scale of damage is the acknowledged fact that points to the likely insurance decision.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces the factual basis for a prediction or conclusion. 'Given the scale of the damage' = 'taking into account how severe the damage is'. The severity (premise) predicts the insurance decision (conclusion).

quests.question: Passengers may carry liquids through security ____ they are in containers of 100ml or less.
quests.sentence: Passengers may carry liquids through security ____ they are in containers of 100ml or less.
quests.hint: The 100ml rule is the formal security condition for carrying liquids.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a formal regulatory condition. 'May carry liquids provided that containers are 100ml or less' = 'on condition that the volume restriction is respected'. This is standard security regulation language.

quests.question: The company will honour the warranty ____ the product has not been modified or misused.
quests.sentence: The company will honour the warranty ____ the product has not been modified or misused.
quests.hint: Non-modification and non-misuse are the ongoing conditions for the warranty.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the conditions for a warranty to remain valid. 'Will honour the warranty as long as the product is not modified or misused' = 'on the continuing condition that the product is used correctly'. Modification or misuse voids the warranty.

quests.question: ____ the strong public opposition, proceeding with the development would be politically very risky.
quests.sentence: ____ the strong public opposition, proceeding with the development would be politically very risky.
quests.hint: Strong public opposition is the acknowledged fact that creates political risk.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an acknowledged political reality used as the basis for a strategic assessment. 'Given the strong public opposition' = 'taking into account the public's opposition'. This fact (premise) shapes the risk assessment (conclusion).

quests.question: She is allowed to bring one guest ____ the guest's name is submitted in advance.
quests.sentence: She is allowed to bring one guest ____ the guest's name is submitted in advance.
quests.hint: Submitting the name in advance is the formal requirement for bringing a guest.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces the formal condition. 'May bring a guest provided that the name is submitted in advance' = 'on condition that the prior registration requirement is met'. Common in event management and venue security.

quests.question: The research project may continue ____ ethical standards are maintained throughout.
quests.sentence: The research project may continue ____ ethical standards are maintained throughout.
quests.hint: Maintaining ethical standards is the ongoing condition for the project's continuation.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a continuing condition for ongoing permission. 'May continue as long as ethical standards are maintained' = 'on the continuing condition that ethics are not compromised'. Any ethical breach would end the project.

quests.question: ____ the success of the pilot programme, rolling it out nationally seems like the logical step.
quests.sentence: ____ the success of the pilot programme, rolling it out nationally seems like the logical step.
quests.hint: The pilot's success is the acknowledged fact that makes nationwide expansion logical.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces a successful outcome as the basis for a logical recommendation. 'Given the success of the pilot' = 'taking into account the positive pilot results'. The success (premise) supports the expansion (logical conclusion).

quests.question: Remote working arrangements may continue ____ performance targets are consistently met.
quests.sentence: Remote working arrangements may continue ____ performance targets are consistently met.
quests.hint: Meeting performance targets consistently is the condition for continued remote working.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces the formal, HR-style condition for an arrangement. 'May continue provided that targets are met' = 'on condition that performance remains satisfactory'. This is typical workplace policy language.

quests.question: She will recommend the product to her clients ____ the trial results are positive.
quests.sentence: She will recommend the product to her clients ____ the trial results are positive.
quests.hint: Positive trial results are the ongoing condition for her professional recommendation.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition for a continuing professional behaviour. 'Will recommend it as long as trial results are positive' = 'on the continuing condition that evidence supports the recommendation'. If results turn negative, she stops recommending.

quests.question: ____ the significant rise in living costs, many households have reduced discretionary spending.
quests.sentence: ____ the significant rise in living costs, many households have reduced discretionary spending.
quests.hint: Rising living costs are the acknowledged economic fact that explains reduced spending.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an economic fact as the explanation for a behavioural change. 'Given the significant rise in living costs' = 'because living costs have risen so much'. The economic pressure (premise) explains the spending cuts (conclusion).

quests.question: The client may request changes to the brief ____ all revisions are submitted before the agreed deadline.
quests.sentence: The client may request changes to the brief ____ all revisions are submitted before the agreed deadline.
quests.hint: Submitting revisions before the deadline is the condition for changes to be accepted.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets a formal contractual condition. 'May request changes provided that revisions are submitted before the deadline' = 'on condition that the timing requirement is respected'. Standard freelance and agency contract language.

quests.question: The new system will perform reliably ____ it is maintained and updated regularly.
quests.sentence: The new system will perform reliably ____ it is maintained and updated regularly.
quests.hint: Regular maintenance is the ongoing condition for reliable system performance.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the continuing technical condition for reliable performance. 'Will perform reliably as long as it is maintained' = 'on the continuing condition that maintenance is not neglected'. Neglect = unreliable performance.

quests.question: ____ the lack of concrete evidence, pursuing a criminal prosecution would be inadvisable.
quests.sentence: ____ the lack of concrete evidence, pursuing a criminal prosecution would be inadvisable.
quests.hint: The lack of evidence is the acknowledged legal reality that makes prosecution risky.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces the legal fact upon which the advice is based. 'Given the lack of concrete evidence' = 'taking into account the weakness of the evidence base'. This acknowledged fact (premise) justifies the legal recommendation (conclusion).
